method: Working time is counted one minute at a time inside a repeating daily window. Every calendar day from the start date to the end date is examined: it contributes only if its weekday is one of the selected ones and it is not listed as a holiday, and then only the part of its window that falls inside the query is added. The query clips the window on the first and last day, so a start of 13:30 on a 09:00-17:00 schedule counts 210 minutes and an end of 10:15 the next morning counts 75. Outside-the-schedule time is the wall-clock span minus the counted minutes, and the scheduled day length is closing time minus opening time. Times are wall-clock readings on the device rather than absolute instants, so a daylight-saving day keeps its scheduled length instead of 23 or 25 hours; the window must end after it starts, so an overnight shift needs two ranges; seconds other than 00 are refused; and ranges longer than 3,700 days (about ten years) are refused to bound the work. Holidays match by calendar date, so one that falls on a weekend changes nothing, and no allowance is made for public holidays you did not list, lunch breaks inside the window, or time zones between the people involved.
